s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of oral and skin lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, associated with a large renal mass and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Sudden warty growths over the lips
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms with papillomatous appearance
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
Sudden onset of oral lesions
Difficulty eating
6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms
Large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression on thorax CT
Invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation on renal mass biopsy

shortlist.label: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of sudden onset of oral and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Acrokeratosis paraneoplastica
shortlist.why_kept: Associated with internal malignancies, consistent with the large renal mass and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma with distant metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the biopsy results of the renal mass and the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by tylosis and esophageal cancer, but the oral and skin lesions are similar to the case presentation

shortlist.label: Tylosis with oesophageal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Howel-Evans syndrome, with a focus on the palm lesions and potential for internal malignancy

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden onset of oral lesions, extensive papillomatosis, and verrucous plaques in multiple areas are characteristic of florid cutaneous papillomatosis, which is often associated with internal malignancies, consistent with the renal mass and lymphadenopathy found in this case.

rejected.label: Acrokeratosis paraneoplastica
rejected.why: While it can present with skin lesions, the primary association is with gastric carcinoma, not urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Urothelial carcinoma with distant metastasis
rejected.why: This diagnosis explains the renal mass but does not directly account for the specific skin and oral findings.

rejected.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome involves tylosis (thickening of the skin on the palms and soles) and an increased risk of oesophageal cancer, which does not match the patient's presentation of oral lesions and urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Tylosis with oesophageal cancer
rejected.why: Similar to Howel-Evans syndrome, this condition involves tylosis and an increased risk of oesophageal cancer, not matching the patient's presentation of oral lesions and urothelial carcinoma.
